seo.title: Self-hosting
seo.description: Run Discord Analytics on your own hardware with Docker: three containers, your own MongoDB, and your bot's data never leaving your infrastructure.

title: Or run the whole thing yourself
description: Same dashboard, same SDKs, your infrastructure. Three containers and a database you control — because "trust us with your data" is not an argument.

compare.title: Which one should you pick?
compare.description: Most people should start with the hosted version and move later if they need to. Here's the honest split.

self_hosted.title: Hosted by you
self_hosted.description: The same images, on your infrastructure.

setup.label: Setup
setup.cloud: Nothing to deploy, patch or back up
setup.self_hosted: You provision and run the containers yourself

updates.label: Updates
updates.cloud: New features arrive without you doing anything
updates.self_hosted: You own the uptime and choose when to upgrade

data.label: Data
data.self_hosted: Your bot's data never leaves your infrastructure

limits.label: Limits
limits.cloud: Account limits apply — see the pricing page
limits.self_hosted: No account limits — they're yours to set

stack.title: Three containers, three steps
stack.description: The website, the API and a MongoDB instance. If you can run Docker Compose, you can run Discord Analytics.
stack.terminal_alt: Terminal output of docker compose up -d starting the website, API and MongoDB containers

1.title: Grab the compose file
1.description: Pull the docker-compose.yml and env template from the install guide.

2.title: Configure your bot
2.description: Set your Discord OAuth credentials, Mongo URI and domain in the env file.

3.title: docker compose up -d
3.description: The website, the API and MongoDB come up healthy in a few seconds.

dashboard_alt: The Discord Analytics dashboard, identical whether hosted by us or by you
